subject: Agriculture
title: Mendel's Pea Revolution
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Mendel's Pea Revolution.

hook.text: Gregor Mendel discovered the laws of inheritance in a monastery garden. Nobody noticed for 35 years.

buildup.text: Mendel crossed pea plants and tracked traits across generations—tall vs short, wrinkled vs smooth.

discovery.text: He found traits followed mathematical ratios—3:1 in the second generation. Heredity had rules.

twist.text: His 1866 paper was ignored. Only after 1900, when three scientists independently rediscovered his laws, did genetics begin.

climax.text: Mendel's principles underpin all modern plant breeding—from hybrid corn to CRISPR-edited crops.

punchline.text: A monk with peas invented genetics. The world took 35 years to notice.

quiz.question: Why was Mendel's work not recognized until 1900?
options: His 1866 paper was published obscurely and ignored for 35 years
